theory: The instruction to use approximation notation whenever a value has been rounded is too absolute: rounding can leave a value exactly unchanged, as in the booklet's question 7, lines 346–350. Clarify that equality remains valid when the resulting value is exactly equal to the original; the worked examples themselves are correct and usable.
